local.heading: Casinos own the Biloxi headlines. Your customers are the people who live behind them.
paragraphs: Biloxi sits on the Mississippi Sound, with Gulfport on its west side, D'Iberville to the north and Ocean Springs across Biloxi Bay. Eight casino resorts operate in the city, including Beau Rivage, Hard Rock and Harrah's Gulf Coast, and the city notes that legal gaming has been part of Biloxi for about thirty years. US 90 runs along the beach past most of them. Search the city's name and the resorts take up a lot of the page.

The other big employer is inside the city limits. Keesler Air Force Base is home to the 81st Training Wing, and the base's own site calls it the single largest employer on the Mississippi Gulf Coast. Keesler Medical Center is one of the larger medical facilities in the Air Force. That brings a steady flow of families who land in Biloxi knowing nobody. They need a dentist, a mechanic, a vet and a place to rent within days, and with no neighbor to ask, they search.

The older trades are still here too. Biloxi's first seafood cannery opened in 1881, and the Blessing of the Fleet still marks the start of shrimp season. Vietnamese American families who came to the coast after 1975 had become a big part of the shrimp fleet by the late 1980s, and some opened markets, bakeries and restaurants. Hurricane Katrina's surge in 2005 wrecked much of the waterfront, and a lot of local businesses rebuilt from the ground up.

So a Biloxi website has two jobs. It has to hold its own in plain local searches like "roof repair Biloxi" against out-of-town contractors and casino-heavy results. It also has to answer a newcomer fast: where you are, whether you go out to Woolmarket or over to Ocean Springs, and how to reach a real person.

industries.heading: Who we build for in Biloxi
industries.intro: Between the base, the resorts and the waterfront, a handful of business types do most of the searching and most of the competing in Biloxi.

items.name: Roofing, HVAC and storm repair
items.body: Contractors working across Biloxi, D'Iberville and Woolmarket. When a storm comes through, homeowners call whoever looks local and picks up first, so service-area pages and a tap-to-call button near the top matter most.

items.name: Businesses that serve Keesler families
items.body: Movers, property managers, childcare, auto shops and clinics. New arrivals check maps and reviews before anything else, so the site needs clear directions, honest details on what you offer, and a phone number someone answers.

items.name: Restaurants, seafood and markets
items.body: Seafood spots, Vietnamese bakeries and family places that feed locals and casino workers off the strip. Menus, hours and photos should be the same on the site and the Google profile.

items.name: Charters, tours and event vendors
items.body: Charter boats, tour operators, venues and vendors that sell to the resorts. Visitors book from home weeks ahead, so the site has to load quickly and take a booking or a quote request without a phone call.

items.name: Medical and professional offices
items.body: Practices near Memorial Hospital Biloxi, which used to be Merit Health Biloxi, plus attorneys, accountants and insurance agents serving coast families. These sites need to look trustworthy on a phone and make the first appointment easy to set.

includes.title: Pages for the stretch of coast you serve
includes.body: Downtown, Point Cadet, North Biloxi, Woolmarket, D'Iberville, Ocean Springs and Gulfport, each with its own page only if you actually work there.

includes.title: Ready for storm season
includes.body: Light pages that load on a weak signal, a tap-to-call number at the top and a short quote form. When weather is coming, nobody in Biloxi reads a long homepage.

includes.title: Written for someone who just moved here
includes.body: Plain answers on where you are, which areas you cover and what a first visit or estimate looks like, for the family that got orders to Keesler last month.

includes.title: Search and ads that report back
includes.body: Your Google Business Profile, site SEO and any ads all point to one Biloxi listing, and calls from each are tracked so you can see which one brought the job.

howWeWork.heading: How we work with Biloxi businesses
paragraphs: We're based in Villa Rica, Georgia, which is a long drive from the coast. So most of our work with Biloxi clients happens on video calls and a draft site you can open on your phone. You mark what you want changed, we change it, and you check it again on the same link.

You won't get handed to an account manager. The two of us who build the site also run the SEO and the ads, and we're the ones on the monthly call. If a Biloxi project needs a visit for photos or a sit-down, we'll plan a trip when it makes sense.

faqs.q: How much does a website for a Biloxi business cost?
faqs.a: Most Biloxi businesses start with our Local Marketing Package: $297 a month, month to month, no contract. It includes local SEO, paid ads management if you want ads (the ad budget is separate), and a custom website valued at $3,500 at no extra cost.

faqs.q: How can a local business compete with casino sites in Biloxi search results?
faqs.a: You aren't really competing with them. Someone searching for a plumber or a pediatric dentist from a Biloxi address gets local results, and Google leans on location, reviews and a complete business profile. A site that clearly says what you do and where you work can hold its own there.

faqs.q: Will you build pages for D'Iberville, Ocean Springs and Gulfport?
faqs.a: Yes, if you take jobs there. Each area gets a page written for it, with the details that matter to customers in that town. We skip places you don't serve, since those pages bring wrong-fit calls and do little for rankings.

faqs.q: What should my site do during hurricane season?
faqs.a: Make updates fast. If you close early, change hours or add an emergency line, tell us and we'll update the site and your Google profile. For contractors, the site should make storm-damage estimates easy to request from a phone.

faqs.q: Do we need to meet in Biloxi?
faqs.a: No. Calls, video and shared drafts cover nearly everything. We're in Villa Rica, Georgia, and we'll come down when a visit makes the project better, like a photo day at your shop or job site.
